newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan activists to hold anti-government protest.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan activists to hold anti-government protest.

text.p: Taiwan activists said they will go ahead with a protest on Sunday against President Lee Teng-hui, calling for the immediate replacement of his premier.

"We are very disappointed by the so-called presidential news conference during which Lee failed to really apologise to the public and replace the cabinet head immediately," protest major organiser Li Tien-chien told Reuters on Thursday.
Lee, in an annual news conference on Thursday, took the blame for what he called Taiwan's worsening social order and gave the green light for hand-picked premier Lien Chan to quit in July.

"What he (Lee) said in the meeting was not sincere and failed to concretely address the problems of the breakdown of law and order in Taiwan," said Li, executive secretary of the Humanistic Educational Foundation.
Some 10,000 people from 30 civilian groups had registered to take part in the march, he said.
"And more are expected to join us to call for an immediate replacement of the cabinet chief," he said.

Premier Lien and his cabinet have faced fierce criticism over violent crimes that investigators have failed to crack, including the gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven colleagues, and the kidnap-murder of an actress' teenage daughter.
Lien offered to resign in July after the completion of constitutional amendments by the National Assembly.
Some 50,000 people gathered in a mass protest organised by Li's group on May 4, demanding a cabinet reshuffle and improvement of social order.
They claimed they had been living in a state of fear because the government failed to improve the social order.
